topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, relates them to histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Discovery of oncogenes through tumor viruses and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Functional definitions and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the classes of cancer mutations and examine how oncogenic, tumor-suppressive, and dominant-negative alterations disrupt cellular regulation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of sequence and chromosomal genetic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the origins, mechanisms, and cellular consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability resulting from DNA repair defects and mitotic errors.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression, hereditary cancer predisposition, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the stepwise accumulation of mutations in tumor progression, how inherited mutations predispose individuals to cancer, and how genetic instability influences tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by confirming learning outcomes, offering recommended reading, and previewing the next session.
